title: P0 edge net scheduler tail latency docket
content:
TL;DR:
A P0 incident impacted hosted API tail latency and streaming delivery in us-west-2 for ~18 minutes on 2027-10-20 between 02:18-02:36 UTC. Root cause: an interaction between kernel network scheduler (packet coalescing/driver interrupt moderation settings on a subset of edge proxy hosts) and our edge proxy batching logic causing request serialization and spikes in request queuing latency. Triggered opportunistically by a brief control-plane rollout (edge-proxy v1.28.3) that changed connection handling timing and exposed a small population of instances with non-default NIC IRQ settings.

What happened (high level):
- Customer-facing symptom: elevated P95/P99 generation latency and intermittent streaming stalls (clients saw prolonged time-to-first-byte or truncated streams with 502s).
- Scope: ~12% of traffic routed through the affected edge shard (single AZ) experienced tail latency increases; global error rate rose ~0.9 percentage points at peak (mostly 502/504). No customer data loss.
- Duration: first detect 02:18 UTC, mitigation applied 02:36 UTC, normal recovery 02:42 UTC after fallback routing and instance rollback.

Detection and on-call chronology (detailed):
- 02:17:02 UTC — Synthetic latency alert (p95 hosted-api generation path) triggers on team-sre-alerting.
- 02:17:24 UTC — Multiple PagerDuty pages; on-call (Aisha) acknowledges.
- 02:18:10 UTC — Grafana: p95 spike from 220ms -> 1.2s in us-west-2 for generation endpoint; streaming open/close errors spike.
- 02:20:00 UTC — Initial hypothesis: autoscaler/queue backlog. SREs inspect router and queue metrics; queue depths nominal.
- 02:22:30 UTC — Net team (Connor) notes increase in per-host tx interrupt saturation on a subset of edge proxies (eth0 IRQs shifting to high softirq time).
- 02:23:40 UTC — Quick experiment: shift a few edge proxy instances to fallback routing (bypass local KV cache) — modest improvement but still elevated.
- 02:28:12 UTC — Confirmed correlation: affected instances show high timer-driven packet coalescing (GRO/GSO) + long softirq wakeups aligned with request serialization in edge-proxy logs.
- 02:30:00 UTC — Rollback of the control-plane rollout that had changed connection handling scheduling (edge-proxy v1.28.3 -> v1.28.2) started on affected shard.
- 02:36:10 UTC — Rollback completed; traffic normalized gradually. 02:42 UTC incident declared mitigated. Post-incident monitoring continued for 24h.

Impact (customers & internal):
- User-visible: increased tail latencies for generation and streaming connections; sporadic 502/504 for streaming clients. Rough estimate: 12% of requests in us-west-2 saw >2x latency increase; 0.9% absolute increase in 5xx across the fleet at peak.
- Business: short-lived degradation for a subset of customers (direct support escalations: 6). No SLA breach for customers on Dedicated contracts; hosted API customers experienced transient slowdowns.
- Internal: ~40 minutes of escalations and coordination across SRE, Net, and Edge teams.

Root cause analysis (evidence-backed):
Hypothesis: A timing change in edge-proxy v1.28.3 altered the micro-scheduling of connection flushes and batching, which exposed a small population of hosts with non-standard NIC interrupt moderation and GRO/GSO parameterization. The combination caused packet coalescence + delayed softirq handling, which in turn caused the edge proxy’s request processing goroutines to queue waiting on socket buffers — effectively serializing what should have been concurrent streaming flushes.
Evidence:
- Kernel softirq and netdev statistics (sar/pss) show elevated softirq time localized to affected hosts exactly during the window.
- Edge-proxy logs from affected hosts show increased per-connection write stalls and sequential flushing patterns (timestamps in the proxy logs show head-of-line waits).
- Rollback of v1.28.3 leds to disappearance of the serialization pattern; reintroducing v1.28.3 on a single canary host reproduced the spike when that host had the same NIC irq settings.
- Hosts with default IRQ moderation (standard vendor image) did not exhibit the effect even under v1.28.3.

Contributing factors:
- A subset of older edge instances had vendor-provisioned NIC IRQ/interrupt-moderation settings that differed from the fleet baseline (missed a config drift remediation patch).
- The v1.28.3 change reduced the internal flush jitter that previously randomized write bursts, unintentionally aligning flushes and making the system sensitive to NIC coalescing timing.
- Runbook coverage for this class of kernel/network interactions was sparse; no quick remediation documented for 'softirq saturation causing io serialization'.
- Monitoring gap: we had host-level softirq/IRQ moderation telemetry, but it was not surfaced on the primary hosted-api dashboard; the SRE had to enlist Net team to find signals.

Immediate mitigations applied (short-term):
- Rollback edge-proxy to v1.28.2 across affected shard (completed 02:36 UTC).
- Emergency traffic reroute to healthy shards for high-traffic customers during rollback window.
- Rebooted 3 affected hosts after applying vendor NIC IRQ moderation fix (config sync).

Permanent mitigations and follow-ups (owner + due):
1) Auto-detect and surface host softirq/irq-moderation anomalies on primary hosted-api SLO dashboard (owner: Liang Zhao, due: 2027-10-29).
2) Fleet config consistency sweep for NIC irq/moderation and GRO/GSO settings; enforce via image/bootconfig and test (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2027-11-05).
3) Roll-forward edge-proxy v1.28.3 with an adjusted flush jitter config (small randomized delay) and gate behind explicit NIC parameter check; add e2e canary that validates softirq behavior (owner: Miguel Santos, due: 2027-11-12).
4) Add runbook section: "softirq/interrupt-moderation induced serialization" with diagnostics and quickfixes (owner: Aisha Kaur, due: 2027-10-27).
5) Improve monitoring alerts: add a composite alert that fires when p95 latency increases + host softirq > threshold in same shard (owner: Dana Morgan, due: 2027-10-26).

Runbook changes (draft):
- New diagnostic steps under hosted-api incidents -> advanced-network:
  1) Check per-shard host-level softirq and tx-packets drops (sar, /proc/softirqs, ethtool -S).
  2) Inspect edge-proxy logs for sequential socket write timestamps and head-of-line waits (log grep pattern: "write stalled at flush").
  3) If softirq > threshold and edge-proxy v1.28.3 is in use, consider immediate rollback of the proxy on the affected shard and trigger NIC irq reconfig script.
  4) If rollback is not possible, temporarily route affected customer traffic to another shard via traffic-proxy rules.
  5) For persistent cases, plan controlled host reboots after config patch.

Post-incident notes (lessons learned):
- Small micro-behavior changes in the proxy can surface hardware/configuration heterogeneity in surprising ways; we need stronger pre-rollout checks that include host-level kernel metrics.
- Our canary gates validated request-level correctness but did not exercise the specific timing patterns that interact with NIC coalescing. Canary tests should include an artificial flush-synchronization workload to detect serialization sensitivity.
- The on-call workflow worked (fast cross-team communication), but we should reduce time-to-signal by surfacing the right kernel metrics on the default incident dashboard.

Open action items (short):
- [Aisha] Publish incident summary to #sre-incident after review (due 2027-10-22).
- [Liang] Create Grafana dashboard panel for softirq-by-shard and wire it to hosted-api alerting (due 2027-10-26).
- [Priya] Kick off fleet NIC config sweep + enforcement PR to bootconfig repo (due 2027-11-05).
- [Miguel] Prepare v1.28.3 canary with jittering patch and e2e test harness (due 2027-11-12).
- [Dana] Update runbook and push to confluence under incident-templates/hosted-api (due 2027-10-27).

Follow-up validation plan:
- After fleet config sweep, run a targeted soak test in us-west-2 with synthetic streaming load for 48h and verify p99 tail stays within baseline under jittered flush settings.
- Once v1.28.3 retest passes, schedule a controlled rollout with staged canaries (1%, 5%, 25%) and require softirq telemetry to be green before each stage.

Appendix: quick debug commands and heuristics observed
- Check softirq hotspots:
  cat /proc/softirqs | awk '{print $1, $NF}'
- NIC stats and irq mapping:
  ethtool -S eth0
  grep —R "eth0" /proc/irq/*/smp_affinity_list
- Edge-proxy log grep pattern used during the incident:
  rg "write stalled" /var/log/edge-proxy/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'
- Temporary mitigation script used (internal): /opt/sre/tools/irq-moderation-fix.sh (idempotent, applied to 3 hosts)

Status and next steps:
- Postmortem status: draft (this doc). Collect feedback from Edge and Net teams, finalize runbook edits, and close when monitoring panels and fleet sweep actions are completed.
- Communication: support follow-ups with affected customers completed; incident summary will be published after internal review.

Notes to self / informal on-call fragments (keepsakes):
- "We almost missed the softirq signal because it's buried in a different dashboard — move it up next to the p99 graph."
- "Vendor images drifted again; need stricter bootconfig enforcement — PR incoming."
- "If you see back-to-back write timestamps with the same goroutine id, that's our serialization smell."

End of docket.
